terms.definition: The health worker at the issuing side hands the holder the credentials the issuing system made: printed (one QR per certificate) or into the holder's wallet, and says what each is. Input is what was issued and the medium; output is what the holder now holds. Performed by a person; the issuing system's own steps are the hcert package's.
Step 2: build and validate the payload against its logical model (DVCMin, or a VHL payload), keeping unknown elements.

Step 6: ZLIB/DEFLATE after signing, and bounded inflation.
Test an implementation against the shared vectors: the PR 129 DVC example, negative vectors, cross-implementation checks and schema checks.
Keep the contract and everything generated from it current: the WIT, its TypeScript view and Kotlin skeleton, the CDDL, and the payload models derived from the FHIR logical models.
Step 7: RFC 9285 Base45, decoded strictly.
Step 4: serialise as RFC 8949 deterministic CBOR, and decode untrusted CBOR within limits.
Check the requirement graph and publish the site that renders it.
The rules every implementation follows: Kotlin first, Rust second, one contract, a synchronous core with no I/O, open standards, no payload in logs.
Steps 8 and 9: the HC1: context identifier, giving a QR-ready string the application renders with its own QR encoder.
Step 1: choose the logical model and hcert subclaim for a use case, from the registry the IG defines.
Step 5: sign as COSE_Sign1 (ES256 or PS256) in two phases, the private key staying with its holder.
Hold the trusted DSCs the host obtained (PEM, DER, GDHCN DID trustlist v2) and find every candidate for a kid.
Verify an HC1 string or raw COSE: the steps upwards, trust lookup by kid, signature, key usage, time and payload; or read it explicitly unverified for triage.

The holder decides what a health link (a Verifiable Health Link or a SMART Health Link) shares: which members' records, protected by which passcode, until when. That choice is the holder's consent, and the sharer issues nothing beyond it. Input is the records the sharer offers; output is the share request. Performed by a person.

The holder shows the one health credential a receiver asks for, as a QR: an HCERT (HC1:) on paper or in a wallet app, or a health link: the HCERT carrying a Verifiable Health Link, or a SMART Health Link (shlink:/). Input is what the holder holds and what is asked for; output is the QR shown. Performed by a person; the library has no holder-side operation.

The health worker at a receiving system scans the QR a holder shows (an HCERT, a VHL carried in an HCERT, or a SMART Health Link) and, for a passcode-protected health link, enters the passcode the holder says. Input is the QR as shown; output is its text (and passcode) handed to the receiving system, which verifies it or follows the link. Performed by a person; never judges authenticity.

Use a VHL: verify it, build the ITI-YY5 manifest request with its HTTP Message Signature, read the manifest Bundle and decrypt each document (journey J4.1). A plain SMART Health Link is received by the same steps, without the HCERT verification.
Issue a VHL: a key, documents encrypted as JWE dir / A256GCM, and the payload as a CBOR map at HCERT key 5 (journey J4.0). A plain SMART Health Link is issued by the same steps with its own carrier.
